title: Operator access boundaries and KMS escrow validation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define an operational playbook and acceptance test matrix for validating operator access boundaries, KMS escrow procedures, and SSO/SAML federation in Private/VPC deployments. The playbook will be used by Onboarding, Ops, and Security to validate that customer-managed key workflows, operator role constraints, and audit trails meet compliance requirements prior to sign-off.

Scope: This ticket covers: (1) definition of operator persona boundaries (kinds of access they get in the private control plane vs data plane), (2) KMS escrow and customer key handoff validation steps including HSM fallback tests, (3) SSO/SAML delegated auth flows and assertion validation, (4) RBAC scoping patterns and least-privilege templates, (5) audit log capture, retention and tamper-evidence checks, (6) handover/sign-off checklist and required artifacts for compliance teams.

Out of scope: Upstream KMS vendor onboarding, platform billing changes, and UX polish on the Console UI. Those will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Operator role manifests exist with explicit separation of duties: operator-admin (control plane), operator-maintainer (limited recovery ops), and operator-auditor (read-only access). Manifests documented in Confluence and applied to a staging private deployment.

KMS escrow workflow executed end-to-end on staging: create CMK, rotate key, export escrow package to secure vault, restore from escrow on isolated node. HSM fallback path exercised and logs show successful key usage audit events.

SAML federation test matrix: IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows pass for Okta and Azure AD test orgs; SAML assertions include expected attributes (email, subject, roles) and audience restrictions verified.
RBAC policy enforcement validated: attempts to access forbidden resources by operator-maintainer fail with 403; operator-auditor can only read audit logs and cannot trigger key operations.

Audit logs for key operations, role changes, and SSO assertions are ingested into the audit pipeline, retained for configured window (90 days by default), and immutability markers validated with checksum/timestamp evidence.
Rollback/playback: Simulate operator misconfiguration and demonstrate safe rollback; automatic alerts generated and rollback runbook executed successfully.
Sign-offs obtained from Security, Legal, and an Enterprise customer representative for the sign-off package.
signoff_checklist: Confluence playbook draft reviewed by Security (security@redwood.ai) and updated
Operator role manifests applied to staging and peer-reviewed by infra-eng
KMS escrow test artifacts (exported packages, logs, and HSM audit events) uploaded to secure evidence bucket
SAML assertions capture (SAML traces) stored and redacted in the evidence bundle
RBAC enforcement test report with steps, expected vs actual, and failing repros (if any)
Audit ingestion verification report and retention policy confirmation
Operational runbook for key compromise scenarios written and validated in tabletop exercise
Compliance sign-off form completed and attached (Security, Legal, Onboarding, Customer)
Release gate toggles and rollback steps documented in Console rollout page
decisions_log: 2026-02-25: Chose to keep KMS escrow as exportable encrypted bundles rather than platform-managed escrow to honor customer key custody requirements.
2026-03-02: Agreed to require SAML assertion audience and role attributes; dropped 'groups' attribute as primary role source due to IdP variability.
2026-03-05: Decided HSM fallback tests to be performed on dedicated lab HSM rather than customer HSM to avoid exposure to customer infra during validation.
